normalization.description: EFFECTIVE privilege as reported by has_schema_privilege / has_table_privilege / has_sequence_privilege / has_function_privilege — i.e. what the role can actually do, including privileges reaching it through PUBLIC or role membership. This is the security-meaningful model and it is the one that reproduces the verified Production anchors.
normalization.first_party_rule: objects in schema public that are NOT extension-owned (no pg_depend deptype=e edge)
normalization.maintain_note: MAINTAIN is a real PostgreSQL 17 table privilege and IS part of this contract. It is conferred by GRANT ALL ON TABLES, so the platform provisioning default handed it to authenticated on every pre-migration-109 table. Live Production at ceiling 193 measures authenticated MAINTAIN relations = 0; a clean replay carried 68. Migration 194 converges it. It is never ignored and never exception-listed.

default_acl_grantee_scope.reason: postgres is the object OWNER: it holds every privilege implicitly whether or not an ACL row names it, and its default-ACL rows materialize as a side effect of REVOKE statements rather than expressing a client-facing authorization decision. Live Production carries postgres-grantee rows on the same four default-ACL entries; they are owner bookkeeping. PUBLIC IS compared, because a default grant to PUBLIC is exactly the fail-open regression migration 109 exists to prevent.

Live Production verification established authenticated MAINTAIN = 0 while a clean replay carried 68, so MAINTAIN was added to the contract and to migration 194. The pre-M194 residual grew accordingly from 186 to 254 tuples. Draft 2 then corrected the 085 premise: live Production shows 085 WAS applied, the rig was skipping it, and once the rig replays 085 the two H-24 function tuples vanish before M194 — leaving a pre-M194 residual of 252 pure H-25 relation tuples.
corroboration: AUTHENTICATED_FUNCTION_EXECUTE 219 — reproduced exactly at BOTH ceiling 193 and 194, once migration 085 is replayed as Production applied it (it read 221 only while the rig skipped 085)
authenticated MAINTAIN relations 0 post-M194 (68 pre-M194) — matches live Production
authenticated relation surface 75 relations / 79 tuples — reproduced exactly
authenticated direct writes = distribution_points + organizations INSERT/UPDATE — reproduced exactly
RIG_MINUS_PRODUCTION at 193 = 252 = 184 data-write + 68 MAINTAIN; the H-24 function residual is {} once migration 085 is replayed as Production applied it

migration_085_status.note: CORRECTION. An earlier version of this fixture recorded 085 as PREPARED_ONLY_NOT_PRODUCTION_APPLIED with its security effect SUPERSEDED_BY_M194. Live read-only inspection of Production disproved that: supabase_migrations.schema_migrations records version 085 (phoenix_revoke_manual_availability_writers) once, its stored payload carries both writer REVOKEs, and the live functions carry 085 comments with authenticated EXECUTE = NO. 085 SOURCE is still a fail-closed PREPARED cutover file and its bytes are unchanged; what changed is the rig, which now APPLIES 085 with a session-scoped attestation instead of skipping it. H-24 is therefore a PG-RIG REPLAY-POLICY FIDELITY defect, not Production drift. M194 is NOT permission to re-apply 085 by hand.
